generation_blocker: Seven targets require the exact evidence gaps and proposed contrast-edge validation recorded below; this artifact contains no MCQ stems or options.

fingerprint_contract.normalization: Join the normalized planned_item_form, physician_activity, learner_decision_token, reasoning_pathway_token, decisive_discriminator_token, intended_key_token, and lexicographically sorted planned contrast-edge IDs with a vertical bar. Target ID and demographic facts are excluded so semantic duplicates cannot acquire different fingerprints merely through renaming or demographic rewording.
fingerprint_contract.set_fingerprint_method: Join target distinctness_fingerprint values in target_id order with a vertical bar and apply SHA-256.

targets.learner_decision: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, a regional ST-segment depression pattern, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise rather than relying on one historical feature.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Syndrome recognition -> territorial ECG interpretation -> biomarker dynamics -> differential exclusion.
targets.decisive_discriminator: Regional ischemic ECG change plus an acute troponin rise in an ischemic context, rather than isolated chest-pain wording, distinguishes NSTEMI from the planned alternatives.

targets.learner_decision: Choose serial ECG assessment and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when initial early tests are nondiagnostic but clinical suspicion for ACS persists.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Test timing -> residual pretest probability -> limits of an early negative result -> serial reassessment.
targets.decisive_discriminator: The tests were obtained early and residual ACS suspicion remains meaningful; a single nondiagnostic ECG and troponin therefore do not justify an alternative pathway or discharge.
targets.intended_key: Serial ECG assessment and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin

targets.learner_decision: Select cautious intravenous crystalloid preload support for hypotension due to right ventricular infarction rather than giving preload-reducing treatment.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Infer infarct territory -> identify right-ventricular preload dependence -> choose hemodynamic support matched to that physiology.
targets.decisive_discriminator: Hypotension with elevated jugular venous pressure, clear lungs, and right-sided ST elevation indicates right-ventricular preload dependence rather than left-sided congestion.

planned_contrast_set.neighboring_choice: Give sublingual nitrate despite hypotension and right-ventricular preload dependence
Give intravenous loop diuresis despite clear lungs
Escalate beta blockade during hypotension

evidence_gap.exact_gap: Current authoritative guidance is needed for the diagnostic hemodynamic pattern of right-ventricular infarction, cautious crystalloid preload support, nitrate avoidance in hypotension/right-ventricular infarction, and discriminators against diuresis or beta-blocker escalation in this exact stabilization context.

targets.learner_decision: Prioritize emergency coronary revascularization while concurrently initiating shock support when acute myocardial infarction causes cardiogenic shock.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Recognize shock physiology -> link shock to acute myocardial infarction -> prioritize causal reperfusion while supporting perfusion.
targets.decisive_discriminator: Persistent hypotension with end-organ hypoperfusion caused by acute myocardial infarction makes revascularization time-critical; temporary hemodynamic support alone does not treat the cause.
targets.intended_key: Emergency coronary revascularization with concurrent shock support

planned_contrast_set.neighboring_choice: Use vasoactive support without urgent revascularization
Defer angiography until shock has fully resolved
Use intravenous fluid resuscitation alone

evidence_gap.exact_gap: Current authoritative guidance is needed for recognition of acute-MI cardiogenic shock, the priority and timing of emergency coronary revascularization with concurrent shock support, and why vasoactive support, fluids, or delayed angiography alone are insufficient.

targets.learner_decision: Select aspirin plus guideline-concordant parenteral anticoagulation as initial antithrombotic treatment for confirmed NSTE-ACS when no bleeding contraindication is present.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Classify ACS subtype -> screen bleeding contraindications -> select the required antiplatelet and anticoagulant treatment components.
targets.decisive_discriminator: Confirmed NSTE-ACS without a bleeding contraindication requires an antiplatelet and anticoagulant strategy; fibrinolysis is not the NSTE-ACS reperfusion pathway and either component alone is incomplete.

planned_contrast_set.neighboring_choice: Give fibrinolysis for NSTE-ACS
Use aspirin alone
Use parenteral anticoagulation alone

evidence_gap.exact_gap: Current authoritative Canadian-applicable guidance is needed for the initial aspirin and parenteral-anticoagulation strategy in confirmed NSTE-ACS, relevant bleeding contraindications/exceptions, and evidence-backed discriminators against fibrinolysis or single-component antithrombotic treatment.

targets.learner_decision: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid transfer to a PCI-capable centre when diagnostic STEMI presents early, expected device time exceeds 120 minutes, bleeding risk is low, and fibrinolysis is not contraindicated.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Establish reperfusion need -> compare device delay with threshold -> confirm fibrinolysis eligibility -> select a pharmacoinvasive pathway.
targets.decisive_discriminator: The expected device time is greater than 120 minutes while presentation is early, bleeding risk is low, and no fibrinolysis contraindication is present.
targets.intended_key: Immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer

targets.learner_decision: Select urgent transfer for primary PCI without fibrinolysis when diagnostic STEMI has an absolute fibrinolysis contraindication, even though expected device time exceeds the usual pharmacoinvasive threshold.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Establish reperfusion need -> screen for fibrinolysis contraindications -> override the delay-based lysis branch -> choose the alternate reperfusion pathway.
targets.decisive_discriminator: An absolute fibrinolysis contraindication overrides the otherwise eligible delay-based fibrinolysis branch; diagnostic STEMI still requires an urgent reperfusion plan.
targets.intended_key: Urgent transfer for primary PCI without fibrinolysis

planned_contrast_set.neighboring_choice: Give fibrinolysis despite the absolute contraindication
Provide medical therapy without an urgent reperfusion pathway

evidence_gap.exact_gap: Current authoritative Canadian-applicable guidance is needed to enumerate the exact absolute fibrinolysis contraindication used in the future vignette and to support urgent primary-PCI transfer without fibrinolysis, including discriminators against giving lysis anyway or abandoning reperfusion.

targets.learner_decision: Recognize post-MI papillary muscle rupture causing acute severe mitral regurgitation from the timing, abrupt pulmonary edema, hypotension, and new apical systolic murmur.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Post-MI timing -> murmur location -> acute mitral-regurgitation physiology -> mechanical-complication diagnosis.
targets.decisive_discriminator: Sudden pulmonary edema and an apical systolic murmur after myocardial infarction identify acute mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture rather than another post-MI deterioration pattern.
targets.intended_key: Papillary muscle rupture with acute severe mitral regurgitation

planned_contrast_set.neighboring_choice: Post-MI ventricular septal rupture
Post-MI free-wall rupture with tamponade
Recurrent ischemia without a mechanical complication

evidence_gap.exact_gap: Current authoritative evidence is needed for the timing and diagnostic pattern of post-MI papillary muscle rupture with acute severe mitral regurgitation and for exact discriminators from ventricular septal rupture, free-wall rupture/tamponade, and recurrent ischemia without a mechanical lesion.

targets.learner_decision: Select an emergent cardiothoracic surgical repair pathway after echocardiography confirms post-MI ventricular septal rupture with hemodynamic collapse.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Confirm the mechanical septal defect -> assess shock severity -> distinguish temporary support from definitive repair.
targets.decisive_discriminator: A confirmed post-MI septal defect with hemodynamic collapse requires a definitive surgical pathway; supportive medical therapy or coronary reperfusion alone does not close the rupture.

planned_contrast_set.neighboring_choice: Continue medical stabilization without urgent surgical referral
Perform coronary PCI as the only definitive intervention
Plan elective repair after discharge despite hemodynamic collapse

evidence_gap.exact_gap: Current authoritative evidence is needed for definitive management and urgency of confirmed post-MI ventricular septal rupture with shock, the role of temporary stabilization, and why medical-only care, PCI alone, or elective outpatient repair are not adequate definitive pathways in this context.

targets.learner_decision: Admit high-risk NSTE-ACS for early invasive coronary evaluation rather than discharge or outpatient testing when dynamic ischemic ECG changes and a troponin rise are present despite symptom resolution.
targets.reasoning_pathway: Integrate ECG and biomarker risk features -> classify instability -> choose inpatient invasive disposition.
targets.decisive_discriminator: Dynamic ischemic ECG change and an acute troponin rise establish high-risk NSTE-ACS even if pain has resolved and current vital signs are stable.
targets.intended_key: Admit for early invasive coronary evaluation

planned_contrast_set.neighboring_choice: Discharge after one reassuring observation despite objective high-risk features
Arrange outpatient stress testing
Continue observation without an invasive evaluation plan

evidence_gap.exact_gap: Current authoritative Canadian-applicable guidance is needed for the exact NSTE-ACS high-risk features that mandate inpatient early invasive coronary evaluation and for discriminators against discharge, outpatient stress testing, or observation without an invasive plan.
